claims.statement: Marketing source captures, generated device frames, and final App Store exports are separate artifact stages, and the Astro site imports an explicit allowlist of frames rather than copies in `LandingPage/public`.

The mobile screenshot runner uses iOS/iPadOS 27, captures English, Simplified Chinese, and Traditional Chinese through `MobileMarketingScreenshotTests`, validates expected counts, and supports scoped device/scene runs without requiring an iPhone for iPad-only capture.

The Mac screenshot runner uses resolved packages on macOS 27, captures production-window scenes serially by locale, requires the app and window to remain active/key through the 2× system capture, validates output dimensions, and backs up replaced captures.

`generate-mockuphone-assets.py` reads captures without modifying them and emits distinct framed PNGs using iPhone 15 Pro Max, iPad Pro 13-inch, and MacBook Pro 16-inch templates at fixed 1530×3036, 2960×2290, and 4340×2860 canvas sizes.
The checked-in App Store delivery is organized into English, Simplified Chinese, and Traditional Chinese directories for Mac, iPhone 6.5-inch, and iPad 13-inch, with boards numbered 01 through 06.

Both platform app icons are layered Icon Composer sources containing Terminal, FrontWindow, MiddleWindow, and BackWindow SVG groups with disabled glass/specular/translucency; the three window layers have a 0.08 neutral shadow while Terminal has none.
The Xcode project selects `AppIcon` as the compiled asset-catalog icon name for the application targets.
The marketing capture scripts keep Swift package resolution pinned with `-onlyUsePackageVersionsFromResolvedFile`.
Mobile marketing captures use a deterministic 9:41 status bar with 80% battery in the discharging state and fixed Wi-Fi and cellular signal levels.

The Mac Workspace marketing fixture keeps the navigation sidebar visible, splits the content 50/50 between two vertically stacked terminals and one full-height SFTP browser, focuses the top-left terminal, and populates the selected nginx configuration view with eleven deterministic entries without a live client.
Mobile marketing capture tests are opt-in via `TERMIND_MARKETING_SCREENSHOTS=1`; by default they capture five scenes, while `TERMIND_MARKETING_SCENES` filters the scene set.

In system-capture mode the mobile marketing test presents each view in a key window, writes a ready marker containing a unique run capture ID and token, and waits for an acknowledgment; the runner ignores stale or repeated tokens, stages simulator screenshots, and promotes them only after test success and expected-count validation, while the test times out on missing acknowledgment.
Without system-capture mode a direct mobile marketing test writes rendered PNGs to the app's Documents/marketing-screenshots directory rather than to repository captures.

`MobileIconRenderingTests` is a separate opt-in in-app UI/icon-label rendering check: `TERMIND_ICON_SCREENSHOTS` selects a language for temporary light/dark and large-type PNGs, while its terminal keyboard size and SF Symbol assertions run even without that variable; these images are not marketing captures or layered app-icon sources.

The Mac debug screenshot launch uses an in-memory store and demo models rather than ordinary persisted app data; the capture test prepares a centered light production window, moves the pointer off content and ignores mouse events to avoid hover highlights during the focused capture interval.

Shared `Frameworks/Resources/Assets.xcassets` supplies runtime AccentColor and vector, template-rendered Linux-distribution artwork distinct from the platform `AppIcon.icon` sources; the distribution catalog resolves detected IDs or like-IDs and host icon rendering uses the selected asset with host/brand/accent tint fallback or a server.rack symbol when no asset is selected.

Mac screenshot demo mode is DEBUG-only and parses a single scene/language launch argument; absent argument uses normal startup, while duplicate or invalid arguments fail launch. Manual demo review supports additional scenes, whereas the marketing runner accepts only its five export scenes.

Mac demo startup selects its requested language and an in-memory SwiftData container even outside XCTest, constructs demo hosts, AI, unrestricted test access, frozen metrics and a demo window, then returns before the normal persistent settings, secrets, sync and live model assembly; ordinary launch and the separate XCTest branch take different paths.

The initial Mac debug demo window is supplied to the real RootView in the production WindowGroup for a nil request ID, while explicitly requested windows use normal window creation; the demo or XCTest disables main-window restoration, and demos under XCTest are not suppressed as ordinary automatic test windows are.

The Mac app delegate sizes, centers and lights the visible demo window and emits a demo diagnostic, but the capture test separately requires a focused native window and emits the marketing-ready marker; the runner uses the latter marker to perform system capture, waits for test success and dimension checks, then backs up and promotes the source image.

The Mac demo path still runs scrubber setup and previous-session attachment cleanup before returning from in-memory demo model assembly; it skips the ordinary persistent settings, Keychain and sync/model wiring rather than all startup side effects.

The site app-icon PNG is a separately exported Icon Composer rendition: the brand README's ictool example targets the obsolete Termind/Resources/AppIcon.icon path, whereas the current platform icon sources are TFM/Resources/AppIcon.icon and TFI/Resources/AppIcon.icon.

The repository-root Swift paywall icon renderer produces light and dark Pro hero PNG handoff assets under Design/Brand/ProPaywall; native Mac and iOS Pro paywall views instead embed RevenueCatUI.PaywallView, so rendering those files does not itself configure or publish the remote paywall.
